consequences: The `Invalid input: ` prefix, VALIDATION code, exit 5 and `details.issues` are unchanged, so callers that read the code or the issues are not affected; callers that matched the old message text would be. `sati task show` with no id no longer answers `Missing <id>`.
context: The 9k command-line review left "no id means the task you hold" out, because a wrong guess finishes the wrong task. Validation errors read `Invalid input: priority: Invalid option: expected one of "low"|"medium"|…`; the core writes that text for the CLI and MCP.
decision: `task show`, `task complete`, `task release` and `handoff` with no id act on the caller's held task only when the caller holds exactly one in_progress task (claim.actorId is the caller). With none or several they refuse with USAGE (exit 2) and list them. Other commands keep a required id. Validation wording changes in core `parseInput` for all callers: Zod's `Invalid option:`/`Invalid input:` labels are dropped per issue, options read `a, b, c`, array indexes leave the field name, an empty string says `must not be empty`. Rejected: a CLI-only formatter (two wordings for one error) and guessing the most recent claim.
title: An omitted task id means the one task the caller holds; validation text is reworded in the core
